text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Over 4,000 people in the mining town of Ndola have had their telecommunication services cut by thieves who stole a cable linking the lines to the central exchange.

- Major opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party have said they will boycott a parliamentary by-election scheduled for February because they are unhappy with the voters register, which excludes half of the 4.6 million voting population.

- A Lusaka court has directed former foreign affairs minister, Vernon Mwaanga, to pay 10,000 British pounds in security costs before the hearing of a case, in which he has sued Newsweek magazine for libel, commences.
- Mozambique's decision to pul out of the Common Market for eastern and Southern Africa is final, the Mozambique embassy said on Wednesday.
